correctness.rationale: For β=α+2>1, the decaying horizontal mode has squared vertical norm Γ(β−1)/(2|λ|)^{β−1}; taking its reciprocal and applying inverse Fourier transformation on both frequency halves gives precisely Cβ=2^{β−1}(β−1)/π multiplying the real part of the complex power. Reproduction normalizes the squared kernel and dilation gives the factor |ξ|y. In the tail substitution v=|x|t the dominating function is t^{β−2}(1+t²)^{−β}; splitting the real-part square and evaluating the real and complex beta integrals gives the displayed positive Aβ. For 1<β<2, the cosine Abelian integral follows by inserting a Laplace representation of u^{−1−β}: it becomes Γ(β+1)^{-1}∫ r^{β−1}/(1+r²) dr, giving the stated sine factor. At β=2, Taylor expansion up to x=1/t and the x^{-3} tail bound make the fourth-order error and far tail O(t²); the truncated second moment supplies A₂=1 times t² log(1/t). For β>2 differentiation of the Fourier mode and Plancherel yield conditional variance (1+v)²/(2β−3); the normalized vertical beta-prime density then yields 2/(β−2). The tail excludes finite variance for β≤2. For β=2, convolving 2|λ|exp(−b|λ|) with itself (factor 1/(2π)) and splitting at 0 and t gives the stated rational-polynomial Fourier expression; the E3 recurrence gives exactly the asserted E2 multiplier, with continuous value one at zero. Independently verified normalization and tail integrals at representative exponents and Fourier integrals of the spatial squared kernel and its true critical marginal. These quadratures only corroborate the exact derivations, not their parameter coverage.
residual_risks: The tail is a power tail in every regime; 'diffusive' is a statement about the leading low-frequency term, not Gaussian decay. The limits are at fixed weight exponent, not uniform through α=0.

value.rationale: This identifies the regularity of a natural normalized tangential smoothing operator sharply across all its admissible power weights. The exact constants, finite-variance threshold, and critical Fourier multiplier distinguish fractional-order behavior from a logarithmic borderline and a second-order law; they give usable benchmarks for other horizontal smoothing calculations. The phenomenon is not a consequence of renaming the known vertical expansion.
residual_risks: Only planar half-space, exact power weights, and fixed exponents; no uniform crossover or higher-dimensional claim.
